description: A single-panel table rendered as an image (Table 2), headed "Alloy | Temperature °C | Hardness (GPa)". The hardness block is split into eight phase columns: γ, α, γ + κ, α + κ, γ + B2, α + B2, B2 Stringer and γ + κ + B2. Two alloys are tabulated — Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni (upper block) and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5 C (lower block) — each with five conditions: Solution Treated, 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C; empty cells are printed as "—". For the 5Ni alloy: solution-treated γ = 4.2, α = 3.1 GPa; 500 °C γ + κ 6.7 (●), B2 Stringer 10.1 (♣), γ + κ + B2 8.8 (●◆); 700 °C 7.5 (●), 10.6 (♣), 9 (●◆); 900 °C γ 4.1, α 2.9, γ + B2 7.9 (◆), α + B2 11.7 (◆); 1050 °C γ 4, α 3, γ + B2 8.2 (◆), α + B2 13.5 (◆). For the Ni-free alloy: solution-treated γ 4, α 3; 500 °C γ + κ 6.8 (♠), α + κ 5.3 (♠); 700 °C γ + κ 7 (♠), α + κ 6.7 (♠); 900 °C γ 3.8, α 2.9, γ + B2 7.2 (◆), α + B2 8.9 (◆); 1050 °C γ 4, α 3, γ + B2 7 (◆), α + B2 8.3 (◆). The table shows that Ni-containing B2-bearing structures are consistently harder than their Ni-free counterparts, and that α + B2 is the hardest composite measured.

observations.observation: The table columns list hardness (GPa) separately for the phases γ, α, γ + κ, α + κ, γ + B2, α + B2, B2 Stringer and γ + κ + B2 for two alloys.
In Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni, solution-treated γ is 4.2 GPa and α is 3.1 GPa; in Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5 C the corresponding values are 4 and 3 GPa.
For Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni the B2 Stringer hardness rises from 10.1 GPa at 500 °C to 10.6 GPa at 700 °C, while γ + κ + B2 rises from 8.8 to 9 GPa.
The highest values in the table belong to α + B2 in the 5Ni alloy: 11.7 GPa at 900 °C and 13.5 GPa at 1050 °C.
For the Ni-free alloy Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5 C, α + B2 is 8.9 GPa at 900 °C and 8.3 GPa at 1050 °C, and γ + B2 is 7.2 and 7 GPa respectively.
γ + κ hardness increases from 6.7 to 7.5 GPa (5Ni alloy) and from 6.8 to 7 GPa (Ni-free alloy) on going from 500 to 700 °C.
Selected hardness cells carry parenthesised symbols ●, ♣, ◆ and ♠, but the table itself does not define them.
The table does not list γ + κ, B2 Stringer or γ + κ + B2 values at 900 and 1050 °C, nor γ + B2 / α + B2 values at 500 and 700 °C; these cells are printed as '—'.
The caption states the table summarises the hardness values for various individual phases and for combinations of phases.
The citing text states that higher annealing temperatures led to an increase in the Ni content of the B2 phase and that hardness values increased for those B2 particles formed at higher temperatures.

The citing text attributes the harder B2 in the Ni-containing alloy to ab-initio results showing Ni-Al compounds have larger elastic constants (C11 221.67-375.61 GPa, C44 116.99-133.21 GPa) than Fe-Al compounds.
The citing text states the results for the α phase and α-phase composites are used together with Fig. 4 to derive the basic trends.
The paper abstract names the alloys as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (wt.%), whereas the table prints the carbon content as 0.5C; the discrepancy is not resolved within the table.

subfigures.description: Two-block numerical table of hardness (GPa) versus annealing temperature for phase columns γ, α, γ + κ, α + κ, γ + B2, α + B2, B2 Stringer and γ + κ + B2; upper block Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni (Solution Treated, 500, 700, 900, 1050 °C), lower block Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5 C (same conditions). Values range from 2.9 GPa (α) to 13.5 GPa (α + B2 at 1050 °C). Parenthesised symbols ●, ♣, ◆, ♠ flag selected cells; dashes mark unmeasured combinations.

unreadable_items: Meaning of the parenthesised symbols ●, ♣, ◆, ♠ is not defined in the table or caption
Table header for the hardness block spans eight phase columns without repeating units per cell; units are given only in the 'Hardness (GPa)' header
No uncertainty or measurement method (e.g. nanoindentation load) is stated in the table
